title: WHO AM I? — AND THE BETTER ANSWER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Moses said to God, "Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?" And God said, "I will be with you. And this will be the sign to you that it is I who have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this mountain."" - Exodus 3:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses asks the question every honest person asks when God calls: who am I?

Forty years ago he would not have asked it. Back then he was confident enough to appoint himself deliverer. The wilderness has done its work — he now knows exactly how inadequate he is.

Look carefully at how God answers. He does not say, "Moses, you have leadership potential." He does not boost his self-esteem or list his qualifications. He simply says: I will be with you.

That is the only answer that ever holds. The question is never who am I. The question is who is with me.

This is the promise Jesus left His disciples when He gave them an impossible commission — surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age (Mt 28:20). The task was too big for them too. His presence was enough.

Whatever God has asked of you, His presence is the qualification.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God asked of me that I feel unqualified for?
2. Am I looking for confidence in myself when God is offering me His presence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I know my own weakness too well. Thank You that Your promise is not my ability but Your presence. Go with me. Amen.
